messages.author: bd61fed06b4f0759
messages.subject: Covariance matrix of ordinal data
parts:
Hi,

I'm quite new to lavaan. I'm wondering if there is a possibility in lavaan in order to calculated a variance-covariance matrix for categorical data. My intention is to calculate just the covariance matrix without defining any model.That is, just the covariance matrix of indicators.

Suppose that I have five indicators (e.g. I1-I5) which 3 of them are dichotomous (i.e. I1-I3) and the other 2 are polytomous (i.e. I4-I5). How (i.e. the code) can I calculated asymptotic covariance matrix of those indicators?

Thanks,
Amin.

messages.author: c1e1212cf2e076c1
messages.subject: Re: Covariance matrix of ordinal data
parts:
You mean more than just doing a polychoric correlation matrix?

If you feel you need to use lavaan, you can probably just indicate:
model<-"
i1~~i2+i3+i4+i5
i2~~i3+i4+i5
i3~~i4+i5
"
model_fit<-cfa(model,data=data,ordered=c('i1','i2','i3','i4','i5))

That seems a little over the top though if polycor will do.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Covariance matrix of ordinal data
parts:
On 03/07/2014 04:41 AM, sami...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thanks Robin for your help. Indeed, I want to save the covariance matrix
> of ordinal data for another analysis.
> I though that lavaan would be a good choice.

> Suppose that I got model_fit, how can I extract the covariance matrix of
> items 1-5?

inspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov

To get the asymptotic covariance matrix of this saturated model:

vcov(fit)

or

unclass( vcov(fit) )

if you need more digits.

If you wish to try out the development version of lavaan (0.5-16), there
is a new function 'lavCor' which will give you correlation matrix directly.

Yves.


Note that is all variables were binary/ordinal, this is a correlation
matrix, not a covariance matrix.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Covariance matrix of ordinal data
parts:
If all observed variables are binary/ordered,

inspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov

will be a correlation matrix (polychoric and tetrachoric correlations).

vcov(fit)

is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the free parameters in the model;
in the saturated model, the parameters are the polychoric correlations
and the thresholds.

Yves.
